# docker_image_search (Data Source)

Searches Docker Hub (or the registry named in `term`) through the daemon, like `docker search` (`GET /images/search`). Results are in the registry's order; the provider's `registry_auth` for that registry is sent.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Search Docker Hub through the daemon (docker search).
data "docker_image_search" "redis" {
  term        = "redis"
  limit       = 10
  is_official = true
}

output "official_redis" {
  value = data.docker_image_search.redis.names
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `term` (String) Search term, e.g. `nginx` or `registry.example.com/team`.

### Optional

- `is_official` (Boolean) Only official images (`true`) or only non-official ones (`false`) (`--filter is-official`).
- `limit` (Number) Maximum number of results (`--limit`), 1 to 100. Default: the registry's (25 on Docker Hub).
- `stars` (Number) Only images with at least this many stars (`--filter stars`).

### Read-Only

- `content_sha256` (String) sha256 of results_json.
- `docker_server_version` (String) Docker Engine version from GET /version.
- `engine_api_version` (String) Engine API version negotiated with the daemon (min of the client maximum and GET /version ApiVersion).
- `names` (List of String) Repository names found, in result order.
- `results` (Attributes List) The GET /images/search response as a nested object, field by field. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--results))
- `results_json` (String) The Engine API GET /images/search response as JSON; results in the Engine's order. Re-encoded, not byte-exact: the moby client keeps no raw body for this call, so this is the decoded response written as canonical JSON (keys sorted, compact).

<a id="nestedatt--results"></a>
### Nested Schema for `results`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String) Upstream `description`.
- `is_automated` (Boolean) Upstream `is_automated`.
- `is_official` (Boolean) Upstream `is_official`.
- `name` (String) Upstream `name`.
- `star_count` (Number) Upstream `star_count`.
